title: Spending on family
tomorrow: Jordan's grandma gives at church. what's Dadi's version?

segments.voice: Yesterday, debt and ease: time for the one who can't pay, and maybe the whole of it as charity. Ease for the debtor. Today, the money that never leaves the house.
screen: `EASE FOR THE DEBTOR.` → `MONEY THAT STAYS HOME.`

segments.voice: A grocery receipt as long as an arm. Rent on the first. A kid who needs new shoes, again. A phone bill for a parent who doesn't know how to switch plans. None of it looks like giving. It looks like bills. A short line in Sahih al-Bukhari says otherwise. The Prophet ﷺ said: when a man spends on his family, seeking reward, it is counted for him as charity.
screen: `A RECEIPT AS LONG AS AN ARM.` → `IT LOOKS LIKE BILLS.` → `COUNTED AS CHARITY.`

segments.voice: Two words in that line do the work: seeking reward. The groceries are the same groceries. What changes them is the intention, the same thing that turned a shift into worship last week. Another hadith, in Sahih Muslim, puts four coins side by side: a dinar spent in God's path, a dinar to free a slave, a dinar given to a poor person, and a dinar spent on your family. The greatest in reward, the Prophet said, is the one spent on your family. That surprises people who think charity has to go out the door. The companion Sa'd, sick and thinking of giving away nearly everything, was told something similar: leave your heirs well off, and know that whatever you spend for God's sake is rewarded, even the bite of food you lift to your wife's mouth. And the Qur'an, asked what people should spend, begins its answer with parents and near relatives before it names orphans, the needy and the traveler. So the circle widens outward from home, and home is already inside it. One to tell a friend: in that hadith, the coin spent on your own family outweighs the other three.
screen: `SEEKING REWARD.` · `FOUR COINS, ONE GREATEST.` · `EVEN THE BITE YOU SHARE.` · `PARENTS AND KIN, THEN OUTWARD.` · then, large: `FAMILY IS CHARITY.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers the people whose food, rent or care passes through your hands, or whose care passes to you. One name per finger, and one thing that went between you this week. Let the count end in thanks.
screen: `ONE NAME PER FINGER.` · `ONE THING BETWEEN YOU.` · `END IN THANKS.`

segments.voice: Spending on family: providing for the people at home, with God in mind, and counted as charity. Even the grocery bag.
Keep this one close: family is charity, when it's meant for God. Home is inside the circle.

howItsDone: Muslims provide for their households as a duty and, with a good intention, count it as charity; many begin their giving with parents and close relatives before widening it out.

chat.meaning: The Prophet said spending on your family, seeking reward, is counted as charity, and named the family coin greatest in reward.

dinar.meaning: a gold coin used in the Prophet's time

Sa'd.meaning: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, a close companion of the Prophet

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a major collection of the Prophet's sayings, by Imam Muslim

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major collection of reports of the Prophet's words and deeds

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 55 (a man's spending on his family, seeking reward, is charity for him)
Sahih al-Bukhari 56 (to Sa'd: whatever you spend for God's sake is rewarded, even the morsel you put in your wife's mouth); see also Bukhari 2742 on leaving heirs well off
Sahih Muslim 995 (four dinars; the one spent on your family is greatest in reward)
Qur'an 2:215 (what to spend: on parents and near kindred, orphans, the needy and the wayfarer)
